paper_000.identified_as: Saintilan et al. 2023, Widespread retreat of coastal habitat is likely at warming levels above 1.5 C
task_relevant_points: Relative sea-level rise (RSLR) and vertical adjustment are central controls on coastal wetland/mangrove persistence.
Paper reports a narrowing safe operating space and mentions >=7 mm/yr RSLR as a stress threshold relevant to mangroves and coral reefs.
Useful for classifying SLR risk in this task.

paper_001.identified_as: Dabala et al. 2023, Priority areas to protect mangroves and maximise ecosystem services
task_relevant_points: Conservation priority analysis should consider ecosystem services in addition to biodiversity.
Relevant ecosystem services include coastal protection, carbon storage/sequestration, and fisheries benefits.
This workspace lacks direct service rasters, so area-weighted service exposure is a transparent proxy.

paper_002.identified_as: Krauss and Osland 2020, Tropical cyclones and the organization of mangrove forests: a review
task_relevant_points: Cyclone impacts on mangroves depend on wind, surge, proximity/direction, previous disturbance, and recovery state.
Mangroves provide coastal protection but can be damaged by severe cyclones.
Supports using cyclone proximity/intensity frequency as exposure, with limitations.

paper_003.identified_as: Mo, Simard and Hall 2023, Tropical cyclone risk to global mangrove ecosystems: potential future regional shifts
task_relevant_points: Defines mangrove TC risk as combining damage and frequency.
Uses IBTrACS category 1-5 storms, 1 degree annual frequency maps, and damage from vegetation index.

Finds hotspots in Gulf of Mexico/Caribbean, South Indian Ocean, Northwest Pacific; intense category 4-5 storms contribute 97% of global damage risk; future 2C global risk change modest (+3%) but regional shifts >10%.

paper_004.identified_as: Kropf et al. 2023, Global vulnerability and resilience of coastal ecosystems to tropical cyclones in a warming climate
task_relevant_points: Frames TC risk in IPCC climate-risk terms and emphasizes shifts in frequency/intensity relative to ecosystem recovery regimes.
Uses wind fields from probabilistic TC tracks and low/middle/high wind categories.
Supports a regime-shift metric based on deviation of recent cyclone exposure from historical baseline.
